title: High-cutoff QCMI shell stress
question: Does the finite QCMI shell signal remain bounded or decrease when the oscillator cutoff is raised, so that a cutoff-independent Gibbs-complement tail becomes a plausible analytic target rather than an untested extrapolation?
method: Build the same zero-source oscillator chain as R-392 from the manifest, but use dimensions 3 through 10 at volume 3 and higher feasible controls at volumes 4 and 5.
Enumerate both orientations of every admissible contiguous core--base-buffer--shell layout with both core widths and all four beta values.
Compute each conditional mutual information shell increment and cumulative value from finite reduced Gibbs spectra, retaining the chain-rule residual and l1 budget.
Group increments by volume, core width, orientation, beta and shell index; retain per-dimension maxima and adjacent-cutoff ratios so low-cutoff growth cannot be hidden by averaging.
Rebuild all aggregates in a non-importing independent lane, apply the product-of-one-site-marginals hostile mutation, and compile scalar profile identities in Lean R393.
finding: The primary lane passes 921/921 checks and the non-importing independent lane passes 6/6. The integrated verifier passes 23/23 with Lean R393 compiling over 13 systems, 54 base partitions, 304 shell rows and 72 cutoff profiles. Every QCMI increment and cumulative value is nonnegative within tolerance; the cumulative range is 4.991889248628922e-07 to 0.009400499834535836, the maximum finite l1 budget is 0.009400499834535836, and the maximum chain-rule residual is 1.7763568394002505e-15. The volume-three cutoff ladder reaches dimension 10. The maximum adjacent-cutoff ratio is 32.000137578349594 and 62 of 72 profiles grow somewhere, with the largest ratio at V=5, core width one, beta one, shell index three, from dimension three to four. Several higher-dimension beta-one profiles settle or decrease. The interacting hostile representative reaches 0.009270624713825448 while the product mutation reaches 1.7763568394002505e-15.
decision_reason: R-393 advances the route by separating a finite high-cutoff diagnostic from the uniform theorem it would need to support. The large early ratios show that R-392 low-cutoff suppression cannot be extrapolated. The eventual settling of selected profiles motivates a two-stage route: prove an explicit energy bound for the spectral complement above a chosen cutoff, then seek a high-cutoff shell plateau. The analytic tail and plateau theorem are not yet established.

adversarial_review.check: All dimensions are read from the manifest and the observed maximum is compared with the declared maximum dimension.
Reduced spectra are diagonalised without clipping QCMI values; negative increments and cumulative values are counted and rejected.
Each increment conditions on the actual preceding shell sites and is compared with the cumulative QCMI through an explicit residual.
Per-dimension maxima, ranges and adjacent ratios are retained, preventing averaging from hiding a cutoff increase.
Both left and right layouts, both core widths and all admissible shell prefixes are enumerated.
The maximum ratio 32.000137578349594 is recorded as a finite diagnostic and is not called divergence or a theorem.
The independent lane rebuilds the Hamiltonian, reductions, entropy and cutoff profiles without importing the primary module.
A product of one-site marginals collapses the shell signal and is caught against the interacting representative.
Lean checks scalar nonnegativity and finite profile identities only; it does not formalise spectra, traces or limits.
Cutoff/source/volume/shape uniformity, Gibbs complement, common core, beta/eta independence, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove an explicit Gibbs spectral-complement energy tail above a chosen cutoff, then test whether a high-cutoff QCMI plateau has a cutoff-independent shell modulus. If the tail estimate fails, register the route-specific obstruction without promoting common alpha.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite high-cutoff QCMI shell stress only. It proves no cutoff-independent shell modulus, Gibbs complement theorem, cutoff/source/volume/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: A finite cutoff profile can identify a scaling direction or expose an obstruction; it cannot turn sampled ratios into a uniform theorem or remove the spectral complement.
